text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTOMATED PAGE fired for synth-checks: apac-probe-flooder group — 5m failure rate above threshold (80% > config 20%). PagerDuty incident created: https://pd.example/INC12345

irene: acked — I'm on it. which probe group/region exactly?

incident-bot: Details:
- probe_group: apac-edge-3
- metric: probe_failure_rate (5m) = 0.82 (baseline 0.05)
- last_failures: 12/15 probes failed
- error: upstream 502 / connection reset in many traces
- sample request: https://synth.example/health-check?id=gen-v2
- runbook: /runbooks/synthesics#apac-fanout

sam: seeing same in probe logs — connection reset followed by HTTP/1.1 502 from upstream gateway. quick log tail:```
[2026-03-14T09:12:05Z] probe-agent-7c9c: POST /generate -> 502 upstream reset (conn closed)
[2026-03-14T09:12:06Z] probe-agent-7c9c: retrying -> backoff 300ms
```

ravi: Could be a bad probe agent build or a routing flap to inference pool in apac. There's a deploy of probe-agent 1.8.3 rolled 10m ago. I'm going to check the probe-agent pods and the routing table.

morgan: quick customer impact check: ingestion telemetry shows ~0.4% of production generation requests routed through same apac pool saw elevated 502s over the last 10m. Most traffic has fallback to other regions; no widespread outage but some sustained errors for low-latency customers. tagging cs/sre for notification. :warning:

irene: I will take PD incident. assigning to eng-sre and eng-runtime. can someone try pausing probe fanout for apac-edge-3 so we stop sending new synthetic waves there?

pagerduty-bot: PD INC-12345 assigned to irene (on-call). Escalation policy: SRE -> Runtime -> ML-Eng.

sam: running pause command now:```bash
# pause fanout for probe group
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  https://api.internal/probes/v1/groups/apac-edge-3/pause -d '{"reason":"automated-page - high fail rate"}'
```
cmd output: `{ "status": "paused", "group": "apac-edge-3", "paused_by": "sam", "timestamp": "2026-03-14T09:13:42Z" }`

ravi: also checking probe-agent deploys: `kubectl get pods -n prod-probes -l app=probe-agent` shows several CrashLoopBackOff on nodes eu-apac-2. I'm going to restart the daemonset.

sam: rolling restart executed:```bash
kubectl rollout restart daemonset/probe-agent -n prod-probes
# kubectl -n prod-probes get pods | grep probe-agent
probe-agent-7c9c   1/1 Running   0     20s
probe-agent-9b1f   1/1 Running   0     18s
probe-agent-crpt   0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  3  2m
```

incident-bot: Action noted: probe fanout paused (apac-edge-3). PD: INC-12345.

morgan: after pause + restart, metric report (5m) for probe_failure_rate = 0.13 (was 0.82). trending down. sample failures 2/15 now.

irene: good — keep monitoring. Please run a small synthetic sweep to confirm stability before unpause. Also prepare rollback of probe-agent 1.8.3 if we see reoccurrence.

ravi: grabbing logs for the CrashLoopBackOff pod — root cause looks like an ephemeral TLS handshake issue with a mis-specified CA bundle in the new build. attaching snippet:```
Error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
 at tls_handshake.go:45
```

sam: opened a PR to pin probe-agent back to 1.8.2 for an emergency rollback. CI skipped, will coordinate manual rollout if we see flare.

morgan: customer impact notes for postmortem:
- affected surface: synthetic checks and 0.4% of gen traffic routed through apac-edge-3
- duration: 09:08 - 09:14 (mitigated)
- severity: P2 (partial degradation for small subset)
- immediate mitigation: paused fanout, restarted probe agents, rolling back probe-agent build as fallback
- next steps: revert bad CA/bundle in agent image, add preflight TLS check in deploy pipeline, add runbook step to auto-pause fanout on similar spikes

irene: I'm handing off to oncall-sre (ravi/sam) for 30 min observation window. I'll update PD and draft a short incident summary for leadership. Thanks all. :pray:

incident-bot: Monitoring window started (30m). Will ping if failure rate crosses 0.2 again.

sam: initial follow-up — alert suppressed and PD acknowledged by irene. will keep thread updated.

morgan: keeping customer comms on hold until we have final postmortem; low impact confirmed but flagging top-tier customers that may have seen hiccups.

irene: closing active mitigation. moving to post-incident actions. last check (09:22): probe_failure_rate = 0.05.

sam: thanks — marking tasks in incident tracker and linking PR for rollback. :white_check_mark:
